feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR National News for reporting across the United States. Explore coverage of economic affordability, immigration, climate, environmental policy, justice and social trends.

entry.title: Homelessness in the U.S. saw its largest drop in more than a decade last year
entry.summary: Homelessness declined after years of record-high levels but it still remains at nearly 700,000. The Trump administration and homeless advocacy groups cite different reasons for the drop.

entry.title: The surprising and often forgotten history of economic populism in Texas
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Austin-based political commentator David Griscom. He authored a book titled The Myth of Red Texas which tells the story of economic populism in Texas.

entry.title: Oklahoma tribes says proposed legal changes puts ancestral lands in Ohio at risk
entry.summary: The Trump administration has proposed changes to the National Historic Preservation Act that could endanger historic sites that are significant to tribal nations across the country. Oklahoma tribes say that puts ancestral lands in Ohio at risk.

entry.title: Housing affordability after the midterm elections
entry.summary: Housing affordability was a big issue for voters who helped sweep Democrats into power this week. Tackling it will take time.

entry.title: Democrats plan to widen their probes of fatal ICE shootings
entry.summary: The killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti during the ICE surge in Minneapolis last winter was a pivotal moment for the country. After Democrats' sweeping wins this week, their deaths at the hands of immigration agents will likely be the targets of renewed investigations.

entry.title: From AC to PA: HVAC tech Chris Donisi wins contest to become the voice of Logan Airport
entry.summary: HVAC technician Chris Donisi won a competition to be the public address voice of Boston's Logan International Airport.

entry.title: An unexpected activist emerged to help block a $5 billion data center in Maryland
entry.summary: Thousands across the U.S. have gotten involved to oppose data centers. One is a Maryland woman who'd been evicted after a pay cut and became a leader of a community effort that blocked a vast project.

entry.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: Vance says they lost the midterms because of ____
entry.summary: Plus: Heidi Klum's hand, hackers and the pope's visitor!

entry.title: Why public schools nationwide are facing a massive drop in student enrollment
entry.summary: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.

entry.title: Former Army medic reflects on his toughest moments helping the wounded
entry.summary: Twenty years ago, Army Staff Sergeant Phillip Trezza deployed to Iraq as a medic. He speaks with his teenage daughter about some of his toughest moments.
